text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear position and repeated claim against driverless cars","quality":"stance clarity","description":"The essay states a definite position early and keeps returning to it throughout the response."},{"evidence":"several paragraphs with a beginning, middle, and closing sentence","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is more clearly divided into an introduction, body, and conclusion, which makes its argument easier to follow."},{"evidence":"“If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault— the driver or the manufacturer?”","quality":"textual evidence use","description":"The essay directly incorporates a relevant quotation from the article to support its point."},{"evidence":"discussion of internet failure, liability, and the car needing human help","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay develops multiple reasons against driverless cars instead of relying on a single unsupported claim."},{"evidence":"“How will it manage to drive on expressways, across train tracks, and even on regular streets”","quality":"reasoning depth","description":"The essay extends its claims by asking how the cars would handle more complex situations, showing more logical elaboration."}]}
